blocks.title: What is the mitigation plan for Harlow Creek?
rows: Odor source survey with the Technical and Performance group: headworks, the biofilter (media last changed 2017) and the biosolids load-out. H2S loggers at the east fence line.
Move biosolids load-out to 06:00 to 10:00 on weekdays; five of the six complaints fall on load-out afternoons.
Return the two complaint calls still unanswered (3 and 19 November). Further contact with the 23 residents goes through Legal.
Send the demand letter to Legal and place a document hold on odor logs, complaint records and operator rounds since January 2024.
Notify the insurer under the pollution liability policy; the policy asks for notice within 30 days of a written demand.
Meet the City Manager before the 8 December council session: the letter, the survey plan, and the biofilter replacement the City has left unfunded since 2023 (section 9.4).
Ask the City whether it received the same letter; section 16.3 allows a joint defense where both are named.
Permit compliance 97.6%. Compliance audits the lab and the process at Harlow Creek; a corrective plan with dates goes to the client before the next monthly report.
Client survey score for the site
Client score 6 (surveyed March 2026). Marisol Vega meets the client lead this month to hear it first hand and agrees three things to fix by name.
Recordable rate 1.24. Review the last twelve months of incidents at Harlow Creek by task; retrain on the two tasks that recur.

ask_answers.question: How is the risk score made?
ask_answers.summary: Every project gets one risk score from 1 (good) to 4 (bad), made from 70 signals in 16 factors.

blocks.title: How is the risk score made?

blocks.markdown:
**Every project gets one risk score from 1 (good) to 4 (bad), made from 70 signals in 16 factors.**

- Each signal scores 1 to 4 on a written rule. A factor is the weighted average of its signals.
- The factors are weighted into two halves, what we control and what we do not, and the project score is the average of the two.
- Under 1.5 rates 1, under 2.5 rates 2, under 3.5 rates 3, the rest 4.
- Red flags: lawsuits threatened; talk of in-house operation or a re-bid. One of these at its worst rates a project at least 3.
- What is at stake (revenue, margin, months left) is read beside the score. It sets which high-risk projects come first.
- The scoring is from your template (Contract_Risk_Scorecard_Template.xlsx), used as written. You can change it on the goal's Plan tab.
